FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: When a remediation fails verification (`improved` is False), `state["chain_idx"]` is incremented, but the state object remains in `_remediation_state` with the original `applied_round`. In subsequent rounds, `rounds_since` will still evaluate to `>= verification_window`, causing the monitor to immediately re-verify the old metric against the escalated `chain_idx`, failing again, and incrementing `chain_idx` until the remediation chain is rapidly exhausted without any new fixes being applied.
PROPOSED_FIX: Delete the state from `_remediation_state` upon verification failure and store the escalated `chain_idx` in a separate tracker (e.g., `_escalation_state`), OR reset the `applied_round` so it stops triggering until a new fix is dispatched.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7
DESCRIPTION: In `check_dispatch_health`, Pathology 5 computes the population mean and standard deviation (`pop_std`) across all individual *round observations* for all models concatenated together. It then uses this `pop_std` to calculate a Z-score for a model's *mean* verification rate. Comparing a model mean to the standard deviation of raw single-round observations is statistically invalid. It artificially inflates the standard deviation (by mixing within-model variance with between-model variance), shrinking the Z-score and making the miscalibration detector highly insensitive.
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute `pop_mean` and `pop_std` over the distribution of model means (`list(model_means.values())`), not the flat list of all individual round rates (`all_rates`).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: In `apply_diagnosis`, if a remediation step has `risk == "DEFER"`, the code appends a new entry to `_deferred_remediations` and returns `None`. Because the `chain_idx` does not advance and no adjustment is recorded in `_immune_adjustments` (meaning damping is bypassed), the persisting pathology will trigger `apply_diagnosis` again in the very next round, appending another identical DEFER request to the queue. This leads to severe queue flooding.
PROPOSED_FIX: Before appending a DEFER remediation, check if an identical request (matching `chain_key` and `chain_idx` with `status == "PENDING"`) already exists in `_deferred_remediations`.

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: In `apply_diagnosis`, if a remediation is rejected by the P-pass, the code increments `state["chain_idx"]` but fails to update `applied_round` (if `state` already exists). Because `applied_round` remains untouched, `_verify_remediation_outcomes` will immediately re-verify the newly escalated `chain_idx` in the next round using the old timestamp, creating a false verification failure loop.
PROPOSED_FIX: When P-pass rejects and `state` exists, delete the state from `_remediation_state` so that it is cleanly escalated without pending verification, OR explicitly set `state["applied_round"] = round_idx`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.5
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager` implements `record_dispatch_success_after_block` and `check_dispatch_health` relies on it to detect dispatch false positives (Pathology 4). However, `record_dispatch_success_after_block` is never actually called anywhere in `process_round` or the surrounding code. Thus, `dispatch_successes` is always empty, and the Dispatch False Positive detector will silently never trigger.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round`, iterate over models that successfully returned a response (or produced findings) and call `self.record_dispatch_success_after_block(model_id, round_idx)` for them.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.5
DESCRIPTION: In `apply_diagnosis` and `_apply_transform`, when injecting adaptive prompts via `per_model_directives` (e.g., for `verification` miscalibration or `add_synthesis_directive`), the code specifically checks `if model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives:`. If a model already has a directive (either loaded from the TOML registry or from a prior remediation), the new directive is silently discarded, bypassing the immune remediation entirely for that model.
PROPOSED_FIX: Append the new directive to the existing one (e.g., `existing + " " + new_directive`) instead of skipping, while ensuring the combined length does not exceed `max_per_model_directive_chars`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: In `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose`, the inline documentation dictates that self-adjustments should trigger if the target metric is compromised "for 3+ rounds" (e.g., `If remediation_success_rate < 0.3 for 3+ rounds`). However, the implementation merely checks `if len(self._remediation_outcomes) >= 3 and success_rate < 0.3`. It verifies that there is enough history overall, but triggers immediately on the first drop of the rolling average, causing premature and highly volatile self-adjustments.
PROPOSED_FIX: Maintain a short history buffer of the rolling `success_rate` and `false_positive_rate` themselves, and enforce that the last 3 recorded values in the buffer all breach the threshold.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.65
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.4
DESCRIPTION: In `_extended_p_pass_remediation` (Module 3), the monotonic decline check evaluates `all(recent[i] < recent[i - 1] for i in range(1, len(recent)) if recent[i - 1] > 0)`. If the recent findings list is `[0, 0, 0]`, the `if` condition filters out all elements, resulting in an empty generator. `all()` evaluates to `True` for an empty generator, falsely flagging a model with consistently zero findings as having a "monotonic decline", which triggers an invalid P-pass rejection.
PROPOSED_FIX: Evaluate the decline explicitly without generators (e.g., `recent[0] > recent[1] > recent[2] and recent[0] > 0`) or check that the generator yields at least one item.
VERIFIED: TRUE
